brief: Renewed US-Iran fighting (a second day of US strikes, Iranian retaliation against Jordan, Bahrain and Kuwait) pushed Brent to around USD 96/b and WTI to around USD 91/b, over 30% higher since the conflict began in February; crude still moves through Hormuz (about 8mb/d plus 4-5mb/d via pipelines) but well below pre-war flows. The same energy spike feeds gold's third straight decline to around USD 4,305/oz: higher oil raises inflation risk, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish message has markets pricing about a 70% chance of a September hike plus two more by March 2027, pushing the 30-year Treasury yield above 5.28% and reversing the decline the Treasury's bond-buyback programme had driven. Separately, the Bank of Israel cut rates 25bp to 3.25% on subdued inflation and a narrowing output gap, with one more cut possible by year-end if fiscal and election risk allow. Turkey's manufacturing PMI ticked up to 48.1 but stayed in a 29th month of contraction, reinforcing the case for further CBRT easing. The credit desk reports a UST-driven GCC bond selloff and new KSA sukuk pricing.
